items.angle: Colleges where graduates earn less than a high-school grad but carry heavy debt, mostly for-profit chains, named.

items.boring: The Scorecard is heavily reported already. Earnings are suppressed for small schools. The net-price max values belong to tiny vocational programs.

items.angle: Which companies report the most spills and releases (Chevron under several name spellings), and which pipelines and facilities keep repeating?

items.boring: These are self-reports: many calls per incident, 378K rows with no company, and SEQNOS 999999 rows are test sentinels. Big operators report more because they operate more.

items.angle: States where the veteran suicide rate runs furthest above the national figure, and which are rising fastest.

items.boring: The VA publishes these rankings every year. The general-population comparison column is empty. The 27% top-1% share is just the national total rows.

items.angle: Which device makers file the most death reports? Dexcom's 376K reports: glucose sensors failing at scale.
items.first_check: Count by MANUFACTURER_D_NAME and EVENT_TYPE='Death', joined to the device brand, 2020-2021.
items.boring: Only 21 months are loaded. Report volume tracks sales and mandatory manufacturer summary reporting, and one event can file several reports. MAUDE dumps are widely mined.

items.angle: Which named employers with the worst injury rates (the ones behind F-035/036/037) went years with no OSHA inspection? Or the reverse: who gets inspected over and over and still has open cases?
items.first_check: Join to OSHA 300A establishments on name and address. Count inspections per establishment from 2018 to 2024 against its injury rate, then list high-injury sites with zero inspections.
items.boring: The NR_IN_ESTAB sum is junk. 30.1B at one OSHA area office and 10.0B at Georgia-Pacific are typed-in sentinels, not headcounts. OSHA also targets by industry, so a site with no inspection may just be low-priority by design.

items.angle: Which carmakers had deaths and injuries piling up in owner complaints about a component long before they issued a recall for it?
items.first_check: Join complaints to recalls on make, model, year and component. For each recall, count the complaints with deaths or injuries filed before the recall date, and how early the first one came.
items.boring: GM, Ford and Chrysler top the injury counts because they sold the most cars. The 99-death and 99-injury maximums look like placeholder codes, and the fail dates run from year 0003 to 2203.

items.angle: Do sanctioned people or companies show up as US aircraft owners, federal contract recipients or SEC filers inside Ripple?
items.first_check: Match OpenSanctions Company and LegalEntity names, sanctioned-only (not the politically-exposed people), against FAA registrant names and USAspending recipient names. Then hand-check the multi-word hits.
items.boring: Most of the 1.1M Person rows are politically exposed people, not sanctioned targets. Single-word name matches are 8% real, so most hits will be name collisions.

items.angle: Which makers recall the most vehicles, and how long after the complaints started? Is Mercedes really top at 28.4B units, or is that a units bug?
items.first_check: Sum potentially affected units per maker per year, keeping one row per recall campaign number. Then compare that to complaint counts for the same make.
items.boring: Rows repeat per component, so affected units get counted many times. That is why the total is 84.2B, far more cars than exist. The manufacture dates from year 0022 to 3019 are typos.

items.angle: Which generic drugs jumped the most in what pharmacies pay, week over week, from 2022 to 2024? Name the drug and the size of the spike.
items.first_check: Per NDC, compare the first and last NADAC_PER_UNIT in the window, and the biggest week-to-week jump. Rank by ratio, keeping only drugs with more than 20 weeks of prices.
items.boring: Shortages and single-maker generics spike for supply reasons, and those are already reported. Per-unit prices also mix mL, tablets and grams.

items.angle: Which gas pipeline operators leak the most gas and have repeat serious incidents? Look past PG&E's famous San Bruno blast.
items.first_check: Group by OPERATOR_NAME: incident count, total unintentional release volume, deaths and injuries since 2010. Rank by release volume.
items.boring: This is transmission and gathering lines only, 2.0K rows. PG&E's 10 deaths are almost all San Bruno 2010, already widely covered. Big operators have more pipe.

items.angle: How many US aircraft sit behind LLCs and trusts with no named owner, and do any link to sanctioned or excluded names?
items.first_check: Count by TYPE_REGISTRANT and by registrant address, to find trust-company addresses holding hundreds of tails. Then name-match registrants to OpenSanctions and SAM exclusions.
items.boring: Owner-trustee registration is legal and common for foreign-owned and leased planes, and it has been reported on before. ZIPLINE's 2.5K are delivery drones.

items.angle: Did federal judges hear cases against the banks they owed money to? A sequel to F-001 (judge stock holdings), with debts in place of stock.
items.first_check: Join judge-creditor pairs to the case-party data used in F-001. Count cases where the creditor was a party while the debt was reported.
items.boring: Most rows are mortgages and credit cards at Bank of America, Amex and Chase. Judges may not have to step aside over ordinary consumer debt, so the hits can be routine.

items.angle: Which sewer and industrial dischargers have missed court-ordered cleanup deadlines for decades? Tennessee permits lead the list.
items.first_check: Per NPDES_ID: count of missed schedule events, first and last schedule date, and whether the latest is still unmet. Join to facility names and ECHO penalties.
items.boring: COMP_SCHEDULE_NMBR is a sequence number, not a count of violations, so the Tennessee sums mean nothing. Many misses are paperwork deadlines.

items.angle: Which commercial or charter operators (FAR Part 135 and 121) have repeat accidents, and are those planes still registered and flying?
items.first_check: Filter FAR_PART in (121, 135). Count accidents per OPER_NAME and per registration number, then join the tails to the FAA registry for current status.
items.boring: Half the rows have no operator name. Most accidents are private Part 91 flights by one-off pilots. Southwest's 77 is a small number for its fleet size.

items.angle: Which US-linked entities in the global company-ID register refuse to name a parent, and do they cluster at shell-registration addresses or near sanctioned names?
items.first_check: Join REPEX to GLEIF on LEI. Filter to US legal addresses with reason NATURAL_PERSONS or NO_KNOWN_PERSON, then group by registered address.
items.boring: NATURAL_PERSONS just means a person owns it, which is true for most small firms. Each LEI appears twice by design, once for the direct parent and once for the ultimate parent.

items.angle: Denominator: Medicare inpatient payments per hospital, which can scale charity care (F-003) or executive pay.

items.boring: The biggest hospitals (NYU and friends at CCN 330101) get the most money because they are big. There is no story in the size alone.

items.boring: Negative values are HUD suppression codes. Incomes are low because that is who qualifies.

items.angle: Which drugs pile up the most death or hospitalization reports relative to how widely they're used?
items.first_check: Join to the FAERS outcome table on the report ID, count reports with outcome DE (death) per drug name, and check that the newest quarter is past 2014q2.
items.boring: The 97% dose share is unit junk: mg, mcg and IU mixed, plus typos up to 5.7B. Known trap: the data ends 2014q2, and report counts track sales and lawsuit-driven filing, not danger.

items.angle: Which universities take the highest overhead (indirect) share of their NIH money, and who would lose most under a cap?
items.first_check: Sum INDIRECT_COST_AMT / DIRECT_COST_AMT by organization for FY2024 on NIH-only rows, then rank the top 25 by dollars and by rate.
items.boring: Overhead rates are negotiated and public, and the 15% cap fight was covered nationally. The retracted-author finding already uses this table.

items.angle: Which receipt lines (tariffs, corporate tax) swung the most in FY2025-26?
items.first_check: Take the September CURRENT_FYTD_NET_RCPT_AMT per line per fiscal year, then compute the year-over-year change in customs duties.
items.boring: The 1,427T sum comes from adding year-to-date running totals. It's macro context that Treasury already publishes as headlines.

items.angle: Which judges or courts write the opinions that get cited most, or least?
items.first_check: Join to opinions and people on the judge, sum CITATION_COUNT per judge per court, and normalize by the number of opinions.
items.boring: Iqbal and Twombly top the list because they set the pleading standard every lawsuit cites. It's a reference corpus, and the Gilstrap finding already came from court data.

items.angle: Which countries added coal power fastest while their clean-energy share grew?
items.first_check: Filter to the fuel Coal, unit TWh, and years 2015-2024, then compute the per-country change and rank.
items.boring: Ember publishes these rankings itself. The 61% share in the top 1% is world and region totals rolled up with countries.

items.angle: Which lenders dominate FHA apartment insurance, and did any insured projects go to owners or managers who are barred or sanctioned?
items.first_check: Group MORTGAGE_AMOUNT by lender for FY2020-26 to get the top 10 share, then join project and lender names to SAM exclusions.
items.boring: FHA multifamily is known to be concentrated among a few Delegated Underwriting lenders (Greystone, Walker & Dunlop). The top-ranked deals are NYC public housing (PACT) conversions.

items.angle: Which credit unions carry outsized delinquent loans or losses against their net worth in Q1 2026?
items.first_check: Map the ACCT_ codes to delinquency and net-worth lines from the NCUA dictionary, then rank the ratio for credit unions over $100M in assets.
items.boring: There's one quarter only, and the columns are opaque account codes. Stress ratios are what NCUA itself watches, and Navy Federal dominates on size.

items.angle: Are federally excluded clinicians listed at community health center addresses, and which centers have the most?
items.first_check: Count rows flagged on the exclusion list, grouped by health center site, then hand-check the top 10 NPIs' exclusion dates against their NPPES update dates.
items.boring: Known trap: it's an address match, not a roster. Shared hospital-campus addresses pull in thousands of people per site (the max is 4.7K), and exclusions may predate the listing.

items.angle: Did quakes near Texas Permian wastewater-disposal zones keep rising after Oklahoma's rise faded?
items.first_check: Count M3+ events per year by state bounding box (OK, TX Permian, NM), 2010-2026.
items.boring: Induced seismicity from disposal wells is a well-reported story. Most rows are global subduction-zone quakes.

items.angle: Which appeals courts or judges run the longest or shortest arguments?
items.first_check: Compute median DURATION by court and year.
items.boring: Argument length is set by court rules. The very long files are multi-case recordings.

items.angle: Which futures markets are controlled by four or fewer traders holding most of the short side?
items.first_check: Take the latest AS_OF date and rank markets by CONCENTRATION_GROSS_LT_4_TDR_SHORT_ALL above 60, with open interest shown.
items.boring: Thin niche contracts are naturally concentrated. The table is misfiled under EDUCATION. The data is a public weekly report that traders already watch.

items.angle: Is the 119th Congress passing fewer bills by close votes than any before it?
items.first_check: Compute the share of roll calls with a margin under 10 votes, per Congress, by chamber.
items.boring: Polarization trends from Voteview are well reported. This is a denominator table for member-level votes.

items.angle: Which members sponsor the most bills that go nowhere, and whose bills become law?
items.first_check: Group by SPONSOR_BIOGUIDE and count bills and laws for the 118th and 119th Congresses.
items.boring: Most bills die in committee as messaging. Sponsor counts are a GovTrack staple.

items.angle: Which operators run mines that went 'abandoned' just before big violation bills or closure orders?
items.first_check: Join to violations on MINE_ID, then compare CURRENT_STATUS_DT against the dates of the last large assessments, by operator.
items.boring: It's a reference table of mine status. The coal-controller finding already covers the violation side.

items.angle: How many rural subsidized apartments lose their affordability rules or rental help by 2030, and in which counties?
items.first_check: Count units where the tax-credit or loan-maturity expiration dates fall in 2026-2030, grouped by state and manager, with vacancy rates shown.
items.boring: USDA and housing advocates track expiring Section 515 loans, and the maturing-mortgage problem is reported yearly. Dates like 1933 and 2098 are placeholders.

items.angle: Which Texas legislators take the most lobbyist-paid gifts, and from whom?
items.first_check: Sum ACTIVITYEXACTAMOUNT, or the midpoint of the range, by recipient official and lobbyist for 2019-2026.
items.boring: It's only 4.1K rows and $136K exact. Amounts are mostly range brackets, the dollars are small, and Texas Tribune has covered this before.

items.angle: No angle: 170 rows from one 2001 quarter.
items.first_check: Confirm the row count against the full CAL-ACCESS dump, to see whether this is a truncated load.
items.boring: It's a test slice, not a dataset.

items.angle: Which water-permit holders sat in significant noncompliance quarter after quarter for years with no formal action?
items.first_check: Count quarters with HLRNC in (S, E) per NPDES_ID over 2016-2025, then join to ECHO formal actions and FRS names. Rank by count.
items.boring: Chronic noncompliance by small municipal plants is well documented and often just late paperwork. Known trap: ECHO's serious-violator (SNC) flag is a constant.

items.angle: No story alone. It's the ID crosswalk that ties EPA program records to one facility.

items.boring: It's plumbing. Top registry IDs are big campuses with hundreds of permits.

items.boring: It's 507 rows for one year. Backup generators after Uri and Beryl is an obvious, reported trend.

items.boring: Battery growth in CA and TX is heavily covered. Only 786 units.

items.boring: SPEND_USD is bucketed ($100 is the floor bucket on 432K rows), so the dollars are ranges, not amounts. Misfiled under EDUCATION.

items.boring: It's a lookup table, misfiled under IMMIGRATION. Small systems violate more no matter what they serve.

items.boring: Big spenders are the party committees and NRDC, and Google's own transparency site shows this ranking.

items.angle: Which named employers logged the most worker deaths and injuries per 100 workers in 2025? This is the newest year, filed just weeks ago.

items.angle: Which water systems serving the most people have no lead pipe inventory (LSLI) or PFAS test on file, past the federal deadlines?

items.boring: States report milestones late or not at all to EPA, so a missing event means the state never sent it, not that the system missed the deadline.

items.angle: Which outside groups poured the most into House races they lost, or into primaries against their own party?
items.first_check: Sum expenditure by SPE_NAM, candidate and support/oppose for primary (ELE_TYPE P) races. Join to results to find the biggest losing bets.
items.boring: Super PAC spending is watched closely by OpenSecrets and the press. Totals are driven by a few presidential and Senate races.

items.angle: Which Texas officials got the most entertainment from lobbyists, and from which industries?
items.first_check: Check whether the table names the official who was entertained. Then sum range-high amounts by that official and by lobbyist client.
items.boring: Only 2.8K rows and $85K exact. Texas reports amounts as ranges, and most outings are $150 dinners.

items.angle: Where are big populations served by systems owned by private or for-profit operators, and do those systems have more violations?
items.first_check: Count active community systems by OWNER_TYPE_CODE and total their population served. The violations part needs the SDWA violations table joined on PWSID.
items.boring: A roster is a denominator. Most rows are inactive or tiny wells, and the 9M max rows are wholesalers that double count downstream systems.

items.angle: Homebuilders' own mortgage arms (DHI, Lennar) lead FHA lending. Do their borrowers pay higher rates or buy at higher prices than borrowers at other lenders?
items.first_check: Take median INTEREST_RATE and ORIGINAL_MORTGAGE_AMOUNT by ORIGINATING_MORTGAGEE_NAME in the same ZIP/county. Compare builder-affiliated lenders to everyone else.
items.boring: Builders buy down rates on new homes, so their numbers look different for known reasons. This is one month of loans.

items.angle: Shadow-fleet tankers under UK sanctions: which ones still call at ports or hold US-linked owners?
items.first_check: Pull the 883 ship rows with IMO_NUMBER. Join to any vessel or ownership table in the warehouse by IMO or owner name.
items.boring: Sanctions lists are well covered. On its own this is a reference list with no money or harm counts.

items.angle: How many new hospices were certified in LA County and Arizona after 2019, and how many share one address or one owner?
items.first_check: Count CERTIFICATION_DATE by year and county. Group by address to find several CCNs at one street address.
items.boring: The LA hospice fraud surge is already a big ProPublica/LA Times story, and CMS has named it.

items.angle: Which counties sit in the worst tenth for both overdose deaths and jailing, and are they getting opioid settlement or treatment money?
items.first_check: List the flagged counties with their state. Join to opioid settlement or SAMHSA grant data by FIPS.
items.boring: This table is our own build and overlaps F-002 (pills vs overdoses). Rural Appalachia tops both lists for known reasons.

items.angle: Which US federal contractors, insiders or donors show up as officers of offshore companies?
items.first_check: Join the officer_of entity names to SEC insider owner names and to contract recipient names. Keep only matches of 2+ words.
items.boring: This is ICIJ's own data, already reported to death. Name matches are noisy: single-word matches are only 8% real.

items.angle: Which Texas lobbyists and clients spent the most by category over 30 years, and who spiked during key sessions?
items.first_check: Sum category totals by FILER_NAME and year. Find the biggest jumps in legislative-session years.
items.boring: Cover sheets are totals only. Spending follows the two-year session cycle, and Texas Municipal League types dominate.

items.angle: Are options granted at a zero or strange exercise price, or dated right before price jumps (backdating)?
items.first_check: Join to the stock price by issuer and date. Test whether grant dates cluster at 30-day price lows.
items.boring: A 0.0 price is often a restricted stock unit, not an option. Dates hold junk years (trap: year 22 and 2047). Backdating is a 2006 story.

items.angle: Which insiders sit on the most company boards at once, and are those companies linked?
items.first_check: Count distinct issuers per OWNER_CIK with Director relationship. Rank them.
items.boring: This is a bridge table already used in F-006. Top addresses are law firms and c/o offices.

items.angle: Which failed pension plans left the biggest unfunded hole for the federal insurer to cover?
items.first_check: Look at METRIC names and filter to per-plan claims. Rank plans by unfunded liability.
items.boring: Rows are one number each, with totals mixed in with details. The 83% top share is aggregate rows.

items.angle: Do veterans die of suicide, overdose or liver disease at higher rates than the matching general population, by group?
items.first_check: Compare the veteran rate per cause to CDC state or national rates for the same age and sex.
items.boring: The veteran suicide gap is a well-known yearly VA report. Rates are 9% filled.

items.angle: Which judges hold the biggest mass-tort dockets, and which MDLs have sat longest?
items.first_check: Rank by PENDING_CASES and the date the MDL was created, grouped by judge.
items.boring: 162 rows. Mass torts are covered by the legal press, and case counts track product recalls.

items.angle: Which subjects drew a surge of Texas lobbyists in a given session, like the power grid after 2021?
items.first_check: Count distinct filers by subject per year and find the spikes.
items.boring: This is context. It needs the cover sheets or the client list to name anyone.

items.angle: Which state agency cases or rules drew the most lobbyists, and who won?
items.first_check: Count filers per docket number and look up the top five dockets.
items.boring: 1.2K rows. A docket number alone says nothing without outside lookups.

items.angle: Did DOJ quietly pull or change Epstein disclosure links between archive captures?
items.first_check: Diff the set of HREFs under /epstein per CAPTURE_TIMESTAMP, and list the links that vanished.
items.boring: Page links churn with site redesigns. The Epstein file releases are heavily covered.

items.first_check: Join to OSHA or MSHA by county and NAICS to get rates per worker.
items.boring: It is an official statistic with no actors. The big rows are national and state totals.

items.angle: Which providers changed owners many times (CHOW_CNT up to 11)?
items.first_check: List the CCNs with CHOW_CNT 5 or more, with names and types.
items.boring: Churn is mostly hospital-system mergers. The 11.1K rows with no cross-reference and the trap on the CHOW flag call for care.

items.angle: Which states' death rates by cause moved the most from 1999 to 2017?
items.first_check: Take the change in AGE_ADJUSTED_DEATH_RATE per state and cause, then rank.
items.boring: It ends in 2017 and is famous CDC data. Useful as a denominator only.

items.angle: Which California lobbying firms dropped clients right before scandals?
items.first_check: Count client drops by firm and date, after fixing the dates.
items.boring: The dates are junk (years 0107 to 5201), 96% of firm names are null, and the rows are form paperwork.

items.angle: Which states and groups had the highest anxiety and depression symptoms during the pandemic survey?
items.first_check: Rank the By State rows for the most recent phase.
items.boring: It is a survey estimate that has been widely charted, with no actors.

items.boring: Rooftop solar follows state policy. California's three big utilities dominate, as expected.

items.first_check: Join PLANT_CODE to the EIA 860 plant/owner tables and rank by owner.
items.boring: It is an equipment list. Solar growth is well covered.

items.first_check: Count distinct end nodes per start node where REL_TYPE='intermediary_of', joined to ICIJ nodes for names. Then name-match top officers to SEC insiders.
items.boring: The same link repeats across leaks. Top intermediaries (Mossack Fonseca, Portcullis) are exactly what ICIJ already published. Dates like 0003 and 5015 are garbage.

items.angle: Which counties sit in the worst tenth on both overdose deaths and jail incarceration: the rural places jailing people while they die of overdoses?

items.boring: JAIL_RATE max of 34.5K per 100K means a small county renting beds to ICE or the state. F-002 already covers overdose geography. It is a derived table.

items.angle: Denominator for water stories: people served per system, owner type and source. Alone, it could show private for-profit systems serving large populations.

items.boring: Most rows are inactive. The top PWSIDs at 9.0M each look like wholesalers double-counting their retail customers' populations. It is a roster.

items.angle: Which Texas lobbyists and clients report the most spending, and did spending spike around specific sessions?
items.first_check: SUM of the category totals by FILER_NAME and year, deduped to the latest amendment per REPORT_INFO_IDENT.
items.boring: REPORT_INFO_IDENT repeats (1.0K) because of amendments and duplicate rows. Texas lobby money is reported as ranges and is covered yearly by Texans for Public Justice.

items.boring: Nursing homes are absent (trap). CHOW_CNT is cumulative since the 1970s. Many CHOWs are paper mergers inside one system.

items.angle: Bridge table for insider stories, already used in F-006. Alone: insiders filing from shared addresses or serving on many boards.

items.boring: Address clusters are corporate HQs (Boston Beer). Row counts track filing volume, not trading. F-006 already used it.

items.boring: One number per row across mixed metrics and years, so the $29.7T sum is meaningless. Top rows are likely program-wide cumulative totals.

items.boring: Rows include national, state and ownership totals stacked with detail, so sums multiply-count. Suppressed cells show 0 (median employment 0).

items.boring: Zero-price rows are RSUs, which normally have no strike price. The columns are renamed and dates hold junk years.

items.boring: 38% null deaths and 91% null rates. Veteran suicide is the big story and is heavily reported by the VA itself.
